title: Arancini
subtitle: with tomato dipping sauce
menu_blurb: Crispy, air-fried risotto balls with a melty cashew cheese center, rolled in herbed panko and served with a bright tomato dipping sauce.
intro: Surprisingly delicious! A crunchy outside, a flavorful inside, and a dipping sauce that pulls it all together.
origin: Arancini come from Sicily, with roots in the 10th century under Arab rule. Arab settlers introduced rice and saffron between the 9th and 11th centuries, and the dish grew out of the tradition of serving large bowls of saffron rice with meat and vegetables at the center of the table. The crunchy breadcrumb coating is believed to have been added during the Norman period, around the 12th century, turning the rice balls into an ideal take-away snack for hunters, travelers, and laborers.

mise_en_place.label: Tools
mise_en_place.task: A pot for the rice, an air fryer or oven with a tray, a cutting board, and a knife

items.name: Herbes de Provence (oregano, rosemary and thyme)

prep_note: Make the cashew cheese the day before, using the [Cashew Cheese recipe](recipe.html?r=cashew-cheese).

steps.title: Cook the rice
instructions: Sauté the onion and peppers in a little olive oil until softened.
Add the arborio rice with 1 cup of water and 1 cup of vegetable broth.
Stir in the tomato sauce, herbes de Provence, sea salt, and both paprikas.
Simmer until the rice is cooked through and soft.

steps.title: Make the breadcrumb coating
instructions: While the rice cooks, combine the panko with all of the coating spices in a bowl.

steps.title: Chill the rice
instructions: Once the rice is cooked, stir in the 3 tbsp of nutritional yeast.

steps.title: Form the balls
instructions: Scoop a tablespoon-sized ball of rice, open it up, and tuck a square of cashew cheese inside. Wet your hands if the rice is too sticky.
Close it into a ball and roll it in the breadcrumbs.
Set on the air fryer tray, lined with foil and sprayed with olive oil. This makes 11 to 12 balls.
Spray the tops with olive oil.

steps.title: Air fry
instructions: Air fry at 400°F for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp.

steps.title: Serve
instructions: Serve with the dipping sauce and a sprinkle of chopped parsley.

sauce.title: Tomato Dipping Sauce
sauce.method: Blend everything together in a blender until smooth.

tips.label: Flavor boost
tips.tip: Add more paprika and salt as needed.

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Use mozzarella instead of cashew cheese.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Keep a bowl of cold water nearby to help shape the rice balls.

facts: 6 to 9 g fat, mostly heart-healthy monounsaturated
nutrition.notes: Significantly lower in saturated fat than dairy cheese.
Nutrient dense and low in calories, and particularly high in antioxidants and essential minerals.
Packed with vitamins (especially C, A, B6, K and E) and minerals (potassium, folate), with antioxidants and fiber for digestive health.
Rich in antioxidants like quercetin and prebiotic fibers, supporting gut health and heart health by helping lower cholesterol and blood pressure.

notebook.question: Is cashew cheese good for you?
answer: Homemade cashew cheese is a nutrient-dense alternative to dairy, typically higher in fiber and healthy fats but lower in protein and calcium.

notebook.question: What’s the difference between cashew cheese and mozzarella?
answer: They differ in nutrition, ingredients, and how they behave in cooking. Here is how they compare, per 1 oz (28 g).

table.label: Cholesterol
table.text: Cashew cheese: 0 mg · Mozzarella: about 15 to 20 mg

table.label: Saturated fat
table.text: Cashew cheese: about 1 to 2 g · Mozzarella: about 3.5 to 5 g

table.label: Protein
table.text: Cashew cheese: about 2 to 4 g · Mozzarella: about 6 to 7 g

table.label: Calcium
table.text: Cashew cheese: low unless fortified · Mozzarella: high (about 15 to 20% DV)

table.label: Fiber
table.text: Cashew cheese: about 1 to 2 g · Mozzarella: 0 g

table.label: Digestibility
table.text: Cashew cheese is lactose-free · Mozzarella contains lactose

benefits.label: Fat quality
benefits.text: Cashew cheese contains mostly heart-healthy unsaturated fats from nuts, while dairy mozzarella is higher in saturated fat, which can raise LDL cholesterol.

benefits.label: Ingredients
benefits.text: Cashew cheese is made from whole cashews, water, nutritional yeast, and lemon juice or cultures. Mozzarella is made from cow or buffalo milk, salt, and rennet.

benefits.label: Melt and stretch
benefits.text: Mozzarella is prized for how it melts and stretches. Some cashew versions use tapioca starch or agar to mimic this, but they rarely match it exactly.

benefits.label: Micronutrients
benefits.text: Cashew cheese is a good source of magnesium and manganese, but lacks the vitamins A and D found in or added to dairy.

benefits.label: Environmental impact
benefits.text: Cashew cheese uses significantly less land and water than dairy production.
